newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hopewell 96/97 interim profit seen week.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell 96/97 interim profit seen week.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings Ltd is expected to post weak 1996/97 interim earnings due to higher interest expenses on loans to finance its Thai mass transit project and China superhighway, analysts said on Wednesday.

"Interim profit should fall...(because of) more interest on higher debt levels as a result of the Thailand project and investment in the Guangzhou-Shenzhen superhighway," said HSBC James Capel research analyst Leon Chik.
"The (interim) result should be slightly higher than in the second half of 1995/96 but lower than its first half," he said, declining to give numerical forecasts.

The Hong Kong-based infrastructure firm was due to announce results for the six months ended December 31 on Friday. It booked a profit of HK$466.42 million (US$57.7 million) for the first half of 1995/96 and HK$302.77 million for the second half.
Few analysts had made forecasts for its 1996/97 interim profit, though many were generally negative about it and the firm's operating profit in full year 1996/97.
"If you talk about operating profit, it's sure to be poor because none of its businesses are doing well," said W.I. Carr analyst Wendy Ko.
Hopewell's US$3.2 billion, 44 km (27 mile) Bangkok mass transit project, currently under development, generates no return at present, Chik noted.
Wrangling between the firm and state agencies has led to serious delays in the project, in which Hopewell said it has already invested between HK$3 billion and HK$4 billion.
The company is also building a superhighway linking Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Zhuhai in southern China. The project's first phase has already been completed and is generating income.
"It is not a particularly good year for Hopewell," an analyst at an Asian research house said of the company's operating earnings.

But the market expects a 544 percent surge in its 1996/97 net profit to HK$4.95 billion, boosted by an exceptional gain from the sale of Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) shares to Southern Co The deal brought HK$10.80 billion cash proceeds to Hopewell, which used them partly to repay debt.
"It's sure to be good because of the exceptional gain," Ko said. "Its interest expenses should fall because it received so much cash... There was a huge reduction in interest expenses."
Chik estimated Hopewell's 1996/97 net profit at HK$4.07 billion, including a HK$3.31 billion exceptional gain from the CEPA sale.
Stripping out gains from the CEPA deal, the earnings would stand at HK$765 million versus net profit of HK$769.19 million in the previous year, he said.
The CEPA transaction was completed by late January and was not booked in the first half of 1996/97.
